# @we64/opencode-vision-multimodal

**Native image, PDF and document analysis for [opencode](https://opencode.ai) — using any OpenAI-compatible multimodal API.**

opencode's built-in `read` tool is text-only. This plugin adds a `vision` tool that sends
**any file** (images, PDFs, Word/Excel/PowerPoint, text, audio, video, …) **natively** to a
multimodal endpoint. No OCR, no page rendering, no conversion — the file's bytes are
base64-encoded and handed to the model, which decides whether it can read the type.

> Maintained by **WE64 AI**.

---

## Features

- **Any file type** — the plugin does not filter by extension; the AI API decides what it can
  process.
- **Native sending** — the file is attached as an `image_url` data URL, the same shape used by
  Zcode and other multimodal clients. Nothing is converted locally.
- **Works with any provider** — anything that speaks the OpenAI `chat/completions` API and
  accepts images/documents (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude gateways, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiMo,
  Nemotron, OpenRouter, vLLM, LiteLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, …).
- **Configurable** — bring your own key + endpoint via config or environment variables.
- **Zero-config fallback** — with nothing configured, it uses whichever multimodal model is
  selected in your opencode terminal.
- **Redirects `read`** — the agent is nudged to use `vision` for binary/rich files instead of
  the text-only reader.
- **No secrets in code** — keys are read from your config/environment at runtime.

---

## Installation

### Step 1 — add the plugin to opencode

From the CLI:

```bash
opencode plugin @we64/opencode-vision-multimodal
```

Or edit `opencode.json` yourself:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@we64/opencode-vision-multimodal"]
}
```

opencode installs npm plugins automatically with Bun at startup — nothing else to run.

### Step 2 — configure your endpoint

See **Configuration** below.

### Step 3 — restart opencode

### Global install (all projects)

Put the same `"plugin": ["@we64/opencode-vision-multimodal"]` line in your **global** config at:

- macOS / Linux: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
- Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json`

It then works in every project.

---

## Configuration

Pick **one**. The plugin checks them in this order (first value set per field wins).

### 1. Environment variables (simplest)

macOS / Linux (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`):

```bash
export OPENCODE_VISION_BASE_URL="https://api.yourprovider.com/v1"
export OPENCODE_VISION_API_KEY="sk-your-key"
export OPENCODE_VISION_MODEL="your-multimodal-model"
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
setx OPENCODE_VISION_BASE_URL "https://api.yourprovider.com/v1"
setx OPENCODE_VISION_API_KEY "sk-your-key"
setx OPENCODE_VISION_MODEL "your-multimodal-model"
```

### 2. `vision` block in `opencode.json`

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@we64/opencode-vision-multimodal"],
  "vision": {
    "baseURL": "https://api.yourprovider.com/v1",
    "apiKey": "sk-your-key",
    "model": "your-multimodal-model"
  }
}
```

### 3. Standalone config file

`~/.config/opencode/vision.json`:

```json
{
  "baseURL": "https://api.yourprovider.com/v1",
  "apiKey": "sk-your-key",
  "model": "your-multimodal-model"
}
```

### 4. Nothing configured

If none of the above are set, the plugin uses the **currently selected model** in your opencode
terminal (its provider endpoint and key from your opencode config). Works when that
provider/model accepts the file type.

---

## Usage

Just ask naturally — the agent calls `vision` on its own:

```
analyze screenshot.png
what does this invoice.pdf say?
summarize report.docx and list the key numbers
read this scan.jpg and transcribe it
```

Or call it explicitly:

```
vision({ filePath: "Images/photo.jpg", prompt: "transcribe all text" })
vision({ filePath: "contract.pdf", prompt: "summarize the obligations" })
```

Every result begins with a header showing which endpoint served it:

```
[vision via custom/your-multimodal-model]

<model output>
```

Per-call override:

```
vision({ filePath: "scan.pdf", baseURL: "https://...", apiKey: "...", model: "..." })
```

---

## How it works

1. Reads the file from disk.
2. Base64-encodes it into a `data:<mime>;base64,...` URL.
3. POSTs to `{baseURL}/chat/completions`:

   ```json
   {
     "model": "your-multimodal-model",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": [
           { "type": "text", "text": "…prompt… (file: name.pdf)" },
           { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "data:application/pdf;base64,…" } }
         ]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

4. Returns the model's text response to opencode.

One HTTP request per `vision` call. Data goes only to the `baseURL` you configure.

---

## Notes & limitations

- **The model must support the file type.** A text-only model will reject the call; switch to a
  multimodal model or configure a different `vision` endpoint.
- **Large files** become large base64 payloads. Some providers cap request size — if a file is
  rejected, try a smaller one or a provider with a higher limit.
- **PDFs** are sent as a data URL. Most multimodal endpoints accept this; a few only accept page
  images, in which case split the PDF first.
- **Audio/video** work only on models that accept those modalities.

---

## Security

- Keys are never hardcoded; they are read from your config/environment at runtime.
- Data is sent only to the `baseURL` you configure.
- Store keys in environment variables or a git-ignored config file.
- Do not commit `vision.json` containing a real key.

---

## For maintainers — publishing to npm

The package is published under the `@we64` scope.

### One-time setup

1. Create a free npm account: <https://www.npmjs.com/signup>
2. Create the `we64` organization: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>
   (choose the name **we64**; free plan allows public packages).
3. Log in locally:

   ```bash
   npm login
   npm whoami
   ```

### Publish

```bash
cd opencode-vision-router
npm version patch        # or minor / major
npm publish --access public
```

`publishConfig.access` is already set to `public`, so `--access public` is belt-and-braces for
scoped packages.

### Verify

```bash
npm view @we64/opencode-vision-multimodal
```

Then anyone can install with:

```bash
opencode plugin @we64/opencode-vision-multimodal
```
